subject: PaymentsCo — residency, retention, and training-exclusion Q&A
content:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@paymentsco.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: Adam Thomas <adam.thomas@paymentsco.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on data residency, retention and "do not train" assurance

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. Before we proceed to legal, our security team asked me to get a couple of clarifications in writing:

1) We need an explicit statement that Redwood does not use PaymentsCo customer data to update or train upstream models (either Redwood-owned or contributed back to any third-party model training). Is that covered by your standard offering, and is it contractual?

2) Retention nuance: logs, snapshots, backups — what are typical retention windows for production snapshots and ephemeral debug logs? Are there any circumstances where those artifacts are retained beyond a customer-facing deletion request (e.g., for backups, legal hold, or fraud investigations)?

3) Deletion process: what does a deletion request from our side actually wipe (training caches, KV stores, backups, monitoring traces)? We need to explain the difference between live data deletion and archival backups.

I attached the PaymentsCo security questionnaire (first pass). Can you please reply with a concise, customer-facing summary we can pass to legal/security?

Thanks,
Ellen
Ellen Park
Sr. Security Analyst — PaymentsCo

Subject: RE: Questions on data residency, retention and "do not train" assurance

Hi Ellen — appreciated the list. High level answers below; I copied Monica (Legal) and Soojin (Privacy/Trust) for any legal/ops nuances. I will follow up with a brief summary doc and a redlined paragraph you can drop in your contract.

Short customer-facing summary (for your security team):
- Training exclusion: Redwood does not use customer request/response data from our Hosted or Dedicated offerings to train or improve third-party or public model weights. We do surface telemetry and aggregate metrics for platform reliability (e.g., error rates, latency histograms) but those are non-content metrics. If you sign a Private deployment (VPC or on-prem), we do not have access to your data.
- Retention: Default operational retention for ephemeral debug logs is 30 days; production request traces and metrics retained for 90 days by default. Snapshots/backups of model state (snapshots we create for upgrades) are retained for up to 30 days unless specifically configured otherwise in Dedicated/Private agreements.
- Deletion: A customer deletion request triggers immediate removal from live stores (KV, object store pointers, indexes). Backup snapshots are scheduled for garbage collection in the next backup cycle; we provide proofs of deletion for the primary live dataset. Exceptions: legal hold and active fraud investigations may require extended retention with customer notification and (where required) subpoena/ court order.

We can commit to an explicit contract clause that we will not use PaymentsCo data to train models or improve our public model catalog without written consent. Monica, can you confirm the contract language we typically offer here?

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Cc: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 11:03:12 -0700
Subject: RE: Questions on data residency, retention and "do not train" assurance

Thanks Ben. Short legal confirmation below for PaymentsCo's legal/security teams:

- Contractual commitment: Redwood will include a clause in the Master Services Agreement (MSA) stating that Redwood will not use, incorporate, or otherwise leverage PaymentsCo customer content (input, output, or derivative metadata) to train, fine-tune, or improve any models outside of a mutually agreed program. This includes models maintained by Redwood and any third parties we partner with. The clause will also enumerate exceptions (explicitly: aggregated non-content telemetry and anonymized usage metrics for platform operation).

- Deletion & evidence: Upon a written deletion request, Redwood will: initiate deletion from production indexes and object stores within 48 hours, submit an execution report, and provide a confirmation of deletion for primary live data. For backups, we will mark snapshots for purge and provide a GC schedule; final purging timeline depends on backup retention windows (we will disclose the schedule).

- Legal hold: Redwood will comply with lawful requests and will notify customers if retention is required by law or by a court order; for enterprise customers we can negotiate a separate legal-hold handling process.

Monica Patel
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

On Thu, 14 Mar 2029 13:26:10 -0700, soojin.lee@redwood.com wrote:

Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 13:26:10 -0700
Subject: RE: Questions on data residency, retention and "do not train" assurance

Adding operational details from the Trust team:

- Hosted API: Requests routed through our shared hosted infra are logically isolated per customer; content payloads are processed in-memory and stored only for the duration needed for serving and caching. We do not persist prompt/response pairs for training pipelines. Operational logs (latency, error codes) may reference request ids but not request content.

- Dedicated customers: you can configure a shorter snapshot retention window and enable immediate snapshot purge following upgrades. For high-security customers we offer an option to disable snapshotting entirely and run with ephemeral state; this is commonly included in Dedicated contracts.

- Private deployments (recommended for regulated workloads): complete control for PaymentsCo — Redwood's control plane can be disabled, and we do not have access to customer data. When customers choose Private, they are responsible for their own backups/retention unless otherwise negotiated.

Operational caveat: telemetry required for diagnosing production incidents may require temporary retention of specific traces (we recommend redaction or tokenization of sensitive attributes). We will include a runbook describing how we isolate and purge incident artifacts.

Soojin Lee
Head of Trust & Privacy — Redwood Inference

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple follow-ups from our side:

- Can Redwood provide a redaction policy or a template runbook for incident traces so we can verify sensitive fields are tokenized before any transient retention?
- For the deletion confirmation, can you provide an example of the execution report you mentioned (we want to ensure the audit trail includes timestamps and identifiers)?
- On backups: if a customer requests deletion, can Redwood guarantee permanently deleting from all backups within 90 days (or provide a maximum recovery window)? PaymentsCo's internal policy requires a maximum of 90 days to fully remove data from backups except where legal hold applies.

If you can send those artifacts (runbook template, sample deletion execution report, and a proposed 90-day backup purge clause) that would be ideal.

Ellen
